Background & Story

Engineer by trade, systems thinker by nature.

A look into how I build software, where I studied, and the ideas and interests that shape my perspective.

I am a software engineer based in Ruwa, Zimbabwe. My interest in programming began with curiosity about how complex structures function under pressure, which led me to complete a BSc (Honours) in Computer Science at the National University of Science and Technology (NUST), graduating in 2024 with a 2.1 classification.

The Enterprise Crucible

For the past two-plus years, I have worked at M&J SERPA, an official Odoo partner. Working on ERP systems quickly teaches you that software is never abstract — it directly underpins people's livelihoods, payroll runs, inventory deliveries, and regulatory status.

Over 50+ production deployments, I specialized in mission-critical fiscal compliance integrations: connecting point-of-sale and invoicing workflows to the ZIMRA Fiscal Device Management System (FDMS) in Zimbabwe and ZRA SmartInvoice in Zambia. In these environments, an unhandled exception or malformed payload isn't a small bug — it halts physical checkout counters and creates tax compliance exposure. That discipline shaped how I approach every line of Python, every PostgreSQL query, and every REST endpoint.

“Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability.” — Edsger W. Dijkstra

Beyond the Screen

I am fundamentally an introvert who thrives in quiet, focused flow states. When I step away from code, my mind seeks patterns elsewhere:

  • Competitive Chess: Playing regularly as knightking_zw on Chess.com. I particularly favor Chess960 (Fischer Random) because it strips away opening book memorization, demanding pure evaluation of dynamic piece coordination from move one.
  • Sudoku & Logic Puzzles: Daily constraint-satisfaction workouts that mirror algorithmic thinking.
  • Reflective Journaling: An indispensable morning and evening ritual for reviewing decisions, setting engineering intentions, and keeping clarity amidst complex projects.
  • Philosophy & Disciplined Craft: Reading Stoic thinkers like Marcus Aurelius, Alan Watts on presence, and historical discipline treatises like Bushido (Hagakure), alongside gripping sci-fi like Andy Weir's Project Hail Mary.
  • Music for Concentration: Intricate lyricism (J. Cole, Kendrick Lamar, Drake), cinematic scores (Hans Zimmer), alternative rock (Linkin Park), and endless instrumental lofi chords during deep debugging marathons.
